# 2025 Tour Championship

The **2025 Tour Championship** was a golf tournament that was the culminating event of the PGA Tour's 2025 FedEx Cup Playoffs. It was played from August 21 to 24, 2025, at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia. For the first time since the FedEx Cup's inception in 2007, the event used a standard 72-hole stroke-play format with all participants starting at even par, rather than staggered starting scores based on FedEx Cup standings. The field consisted of the top 30 players in the FedEx Cup points list following the BMW Championship. England's Tommy Fleetwood won the tournament at 18 under par, three strokes ahead of Russell Henley and Patrick Cantlay, securing his first PGA Tour title and the FedEx Cup championship.

## Format and qualification

The Tour Championship serves as the final event in the PGA Tour's FedEx Cup Playoffs, a series of three tournaments that determine the season-long FedEx Cup champion. In 2025, the PGA Tour implemented a change to the tournament's format, shifting from a system where players began with starting strokes based on their FedEx Cup positions to a traditional 72-hole stroke-play competition where all entrants started at even par. This adjustment aimed to emphasize performance over the four rounds while maintaining the event's role in crowning the FedEx Cup winner. The winner of the Tour Championship also received the FedEx Cup and its associated bonus payout.

The field was limited to the top 30 players in the FedEx Cup standings after the conclusion of the BMW Championship, the second playoff event. Qualification for the playoffs began with the top 70 players after the regular season's Wyndham Championship advancing to the FedEx St. Jude Championship, followed by the top 50 proceeding to the BMW Championship. The Tour Championship field represented players who had accumulated the highest points throughout the season, with points awarded based on performance in regular-season events and the first two playoff tournaments.

The 2025 field included five former FedEx Cup champions: Scottie Scheffler (2024), Rory McIlroy (2016, 2019, 2022), Justin Rose (2018), Justin Thomas (2017), and Patrick Cantlay (2021). The players were (in alphabetical order): Ludvig Åberg, Akshay Bhatia, Keegan Bradley, Jacob Bridgeman, Sam Burns, Patrick Cantlay, Corey Conners, Harris English, Tommy Fleetwood, Chris Gotterup, Ben Griffin, Harry Hall, Brian Harman, Russell Henley, Viktor Hovland, Sungjae Im, Shane Lowry, Robert MacIntyre, Hideki Matsuyama, Rory McIlroy, Maverick McNealy, Collin Morikawa, Andrew Novak, Justin Rose, Scottie Scheffler, J.J. Spaun, Sepp Straka, Nick Taylor, Justin Thomas, and Cameron Young.

## Course

The tournament was held at East Lake Golf Club, a par-70 course measuring 7,490 yards (6,850 m). The layout featured adjustments in 2025 to promote more risk-reward opportunities, with the intent of producing winning scores closer to par and enhancing competitive drama. East Lake has hosted the Tour Championship annually since 2004.

## Tournament summary

### First round

Russell Henley took the lead with a nine-under-par 61, which included nine birdies and no bogeys. Scottie Scheffler finished two strokes behind at seven under par after a bogey-free round that featured three birdies in his last four holes and a par save on the 16th hole. Seven players tied for third at six under par: Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Patrick Cantlay, Robert MacIntyre, and Tommy Fleetwood. Rory McIlroy ended the day at four under par, highlighted by an eagle on the par-five sixth hole and a birdie on the 18th after his bunker shot deflected off a grandstand.

### Second round

Tommy Fleetwood carded a seven-under-par 63 to tie Russell Henley for the lead at 13 under par. Henley's four-under 66 included birdies on holes 3, 5, 8, and 17. Scottie Scheffler remained in contention at 10 under par overall after a three-under round.

### Third round

Patrick Cantlay posted a six-under-par 64 to join Tommy Fleetwood atop the leaderboard at 16 under par. Fleetwood scored a three-under 67. Keegan Bradley and Scottie Scheffler were among those trailing closely.

### Fourth round

Tommy Fleetwood shot a two-under-par 68 to finish at 18 under par and win by three strokes. His round included birdies on holes 3, 8, 9, 15, 16, and 17, offset by bogeys on holes 11 and 13. Key moments featured a flop shot from the fringe on the third hole, a bunker save on the seventh, and precise iron approaches on the closing holes. Russell Henley and Patrick Cantlay tied for second at 15 under par.

Written by Staff 

Effective in 2025, the TOUR Championship will be played as a 72-hole stroke-play event, with all players starting the tournament at even par. The best performer over the course of four rounds at the TOUR Championship will win the FedExCup.

The PGA TOUR announced three meaningful changes to the TOUR Championship as part of its ongoing commitment to accelerate innovation on behalf of fans through the [Fan Forward](https://www.pgatour.com/fanforward?deviceId=7c1cbb47-a98f-4237-9b6d-b2fdf72d4192&deviceId=d9a10f2c-de54-4f93-b794-142b0c3b1f3d) initiative:

*   **Elimination of Starting Strokes:** The TOUR Championship will be played as a 72-hole stroke-play event, with all players starting the tournament at even par. The best performer over the course of four rounds at the TOUR Championship will win the FedExCup.
*   **Adjustments to course setup:** In response to data indicating fans want to see winning scores closer to par, the PGA TOUR Rules Committee will adjust its course setup approach to encourage more risk/reward moments throughout each round, further heightening the drama and competition to determine the FedExCup champion.
*   **Toughest tournament to qualify for:** Already the most elite field in golf, the TOUR Championship field size will remain at 30 players in 2025. The Player Advisory Council is studying the qualification system of future years to raise the stakes on the entire FedExCup season and reinforce the TOUR Championship as the hardest tournament to qualify for.

### Who qualified for the TOUR Championship?

The top 30 players at the conclusion of the BMW Championship advance to the TOUR Championship. Led by none other than defending FedExCup champion and newly crowned BMW Championship winner Scottie Scheffler, see the [30 players who qualified for the TOUR Championship here](https://www.pgatour.com/article/news/inside-the-field/2025/08/17/see-whos-playing-tour-championship-atlanta-east-lake-fedexcup-playoffs-scottie-scheffler-rory-mcilroy?deviceId=d9a10f2c-de54-4f93-b794-142b0c3b1f3d).

**ATLANTA —** The field is set for the 2025 TOUR Championship with the top 30 players in the FedExCup qualifying for the season finale at East Lake Golf Club. Reigning FedExCup Champion Scottie Scheffler earned his 18th win of his PGA TOUR career and his fifth victory of the 2025 season at the BMW Championship, maintaining his place as the FedExCup leader for the fourth consecutive season as he seeks to become the first back-to-back FedExCup Champion.

Rory McIlroy, who won the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am, THE PLAYERS Championship and the Masters Tournament this season, collected a T12 finish at Caves Valley Golf Club and will enter the week at No. 2 in the FedExCup. J.J. Spaun, who earned his second TOUR title in dramatic fashion at the U.S. Open at Oakmont, enters at No. 3 while 2018 FedExCup Champion Justin Rose sits at No. 4 following his victory at the first Playoffs event, the FedEx St. Jude Championship. Tommy Fleetwood finished T4 at the BMW Championship and rounds out the top five in the standings.

The FedExCup Playoffs conclude this week at the TOUR Championship, supported by Proud Partners Accenture, Coca-Cola and Southern Company, where the top 30 players will compete for the title of 2025 FedExCup Champion. The first and second rounds will be broadcast live on Golf Channel from historic East Lake Golf Club on Thursday, Aug. 21 and Friday, Aug. 22 from 1-6 p.m. The third round will be broadcast on Golf Channel from 1-2:30 p.m. and on NBC from 2:30-7 p.m. on Saturday, Aug. 23, with the final round slated for Sunday, Aug. 24 from 12-1:30 p.m. on Golf Channel and 1:30-6 p.m. on NBC.

As previously announced, the TOUR Championship will be played as a 72-hole stroke-play event, with all players starting the tournament at even par and the winner claiming the FedExCup.

Other Player Storylines:
------------------------

*   Reigning FedExCup Champion Scottie Scheffler (No. 1) holds the FedExCup lead entering the TOUR Championship for the fourth consecutive year (T2/2022; T6/2023; 1st/2024). Scheffler looks to become the first back-to-back FedExCup Champion.
*   Harry Hall (No. 45 to No. 26) was the only player to begin the BMW Championship outside the top 30 in the FedExCup and play his way into the TOUR Championship following his sixth-place finish at Caves Valley.
*   Seven players are making their TOUR Championship debut:
    *   J.J. Spaun (No. 3)
    *   Ben Griffin (No. 6)
    *   Maverick McNealy (No. 10)
    *   Andrew Novak (No. 15)
    *   Harry Hall (No. 26)
    *   Jacob Bridgeman (No. 27)
    *   Chris Gotterup (No. 29)
*   Six former FedExCup Champions qualified for the TOUR Championship: No. 1 Scottie Scheffler (2024), No. 2 Rory McIlroy (2016, 2019, 2022), No. 4 Justin Rose (2018), No. 12 Justin Thomas (2017), No. 20 Patrick Cantlay (2021), No. 22 Viktor Hovland (2023).
*   Rory McIlroy qualified for his eighth consecutive TOUR Championship, the longest active streak. Tony Finau and Xander Schauffele entered the Playoffs sharing the longest active streak (8) before failing to advance past the FedEx St. Jude Championship and BMW Championship, respectively.

2025 Tour Championship Full Field: FedEx Cup, $10 Million Up for Grabs for Final 30
===================================================================================

The PGA Tour’s season finale no longer has its starting-strokes format, meaning all 30 players begin on equal footing at East Lake.

#### [John Schwarb](https://www.si.com/author/john-schwarb) | Aug 18, 2025

![Image 2: East Lake Golf Club again hosts the Tour Championship.](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_crop,w_6000,h_3375,x_0,y_418/c_fill,w_720,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/images/ImagnImages/mmsport/si/01k2yy58g1ypn9ddsefg.jpg)

East Lake Golf Club again hosts the Tour Championship. / John David Mercer-Imagn Images

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fgolf%2F2025-tour-championship-full-field-fedex-cup-final-30)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=2025%20Tour%20Championship%20Full%20Field:%20FedEx%20Cup%2C%20$10%20Million%20Up%20for%20Grabs%20for%20Final%2030&url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fgolf%2F2025-tour-championship-full-field-fedex-cup-final-30)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fwww.si.com%2Fgolf%2F2025-tour-championship-full-field-fedex-cup-final-30&title=2025%20Tour%20Championship%20Full%20Field:%20FedEx%20Cup%2C%20$10%20Million%20Up%20for%20Grabs%20for%20Final%2030)

* * *

The PGA Tour’s 2025 season finale is here, and this time the handicap is gone.

For the last six years, the FedEx Cup points leader started the Tour Championship at 10 under, a cushion granted for a season’s (and two playoff events) worth of work. Those barely squeaking in the final 30 started at even par and essentially had no shot at the top prize.

Now, the Tour has scrapped its so-called starting-strokes format and it’s anyone’s ballgame at East Lake. Or at least in theory.

Scottie Scheffler is the defending champion, winning by four shots a year ago with his 10 under head start. He has won five times in 2025, from major-championship routs to a thrilling [comeback win last week at the BMW Championship](https://www.si.com/golf/scottie-scheffler-comeback-win-bmw-championship), and is an absurd +150 at DraftKings to win this week.

Who might beat him? Rory McIlroy has won three times at East Lake (and hence three FedEx Cups), including once before the starting-strokes era. Viktor Hovland (2023) and Patrick Cantlay (2021) are also past champions in the field. Justin Rose won the first playoff event two weeks ago, where Scheffler finished one shot out of a playoff. The ultimate long shot might be Harry Hall, the only player to [break into the top 30 via the BMW](https://www.si.com/golf/rickie-fowler-fumbles-tour-championship-berth-late-bmw-harry-hall-makes).

The winner’s take is $10 million this week, down from previous years as the Tour opted to shift some of the FedEx Cup bonus pool to earlier in the playoffs—like the $5 million Scheffler just won for being the points leader after the BMW, money he had clinched even before playing.
